newsitem.title: UK: VLCC rates stay soft but higher than last year.
newsitem.headline: VLCC rates stay soft but higher than last year.

text.p: Very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates softened this week on ample tonnage even though the number of fixtures done was above average for the time of year, brokers said on Friday.

E.A. Gibson Shipbrokers in their weekly tanker report noted healthy demand for large tonnage from the Middle East Gulf and said the fall in rates was probably due to the appearance of Far Eastern oil company relets.
Galbraith's Ltd said there had been over 40 VLCC deals this week, well above average, with a very healthy tonnage list from a charterer's point of view, even for modern tonnage.

"We cannot expect next week to be quite as busy...but surely owners with tonnage left must feel a little more confident and should be able to hold (VLCC) rates at present levels," they added in their weekly tanker report.

They said that while VLCC rates had fallen this week, ultra-large crude carriers (ULCCs) had scored well due to tight availability, with a 400,000 tonne vessel fetching W52.5 Mideast/USG, more than could have been expected of a VLCC on this route.
In a separate table, Galbraith's showed Middle East VLCC rates to be substantially above this week last year, with Mideast/UKC, for example, now at W55.00 against W50.00 a year ago.
Mideast/Japan VLCCs were little changed at W52.5 on Friday, with Mideast/Red Sea at W55, while West Africa/USG voyages were at about W70 in a busy market.
West Africa 130,000 tonne vessels (Suezmaxes) suffered in consequence and at W95 were some five points down on the week with further slippage likely next week, brokers said.
In the cross-Mediterranean market, the 130,000 tonne sector was quiet with rates dropping from around W97.5 last week to W85, while 80,000 tonne vessels held steady at around W125.
"This represents a drop of about five Worldscale points but business is scarce and the pressure is on owners to maintain this level," Galbraith's said.
In the cross-North Sea market, 80,000 tonne cargoes fell to W115 on Friday from W120 at the beginning of the week and after reaching W140 last week.
Caribs/upcoast 70,000 tonne rates remained extremely firm at W230 -- 100 points above the February average of W131.6, according to data on Rigos Chartering Inc's Internet site.
But some brokers said a decision by the Venezuelan authorities to postpone a ban on single-hulled vessels in Lake Macaraibo for five years could have a dampening effect on Caribbean rates.
